`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8701-i18n-key-boundary-pack-sweep`

Dispatched by the PM seat. Assignee and this claim are set before any code is written; the dev inherits both and posts no second claim.

## The ruling

**Take the boundary fix for the pack sweep** — the mechanism PR #8699 already built and defaulted off. The one-line half is not the deliverable, though; the measurement obligation this card names is.

⛔ **Re-tiering without re-measuring is the thing to avoid.** objectui#4658's dispatch ruling rests on a **measured false-positive rate for the pack sweep**, taken under the current behaviour. Flipping the boundary moves that reading. So the PR must restate the rate under the new behaviour and say whether #4658's ruling still stands on it — that is the part a later reader will need and the part that is expensive to reconstruct.

**Classify all 13, delete none.** Each of the 13 has to be read and put in one of two buckets — genuinely dead, or live but unevidenced by this instrument — with the evidence for each. ⛔ No key is deleted in this PR: a dead i18n key is a per-key decision with its own risk, and mixing "the instrument was wrong" with "and here are 13 deletions" makes both harder to review. If the classification finds genuinely dead keys, that is a **finding to file**, and it is a good outcome — the card is right that this may *find* work rather than only tidy a tier.

⚠️ **The two probes are not the same problem, and the card says why.** `occursAtPropertyBoundary` guards the *chain* probe by refusing a next character that continues an identifier — and it would **not** be sufficient here, because `.` is not an identifier character, so `ns.group.leaf` followed by `.detail` sails through it. The boundary class the full-key probe needs is the card's: bounded on both sides by a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_$.-]`. ⛔ Do not reuse the chain-probe guard on the assumption that a boundary is a boundary.

**One check the card does not ask for**: it reports the 13 are identical whether the property-chain probe is on or off, so the artefact is isolated. Confirm that still holds after your change rather than inheriting it — if the two legs start interacting, the isolation claim in the card stops being true and the report should say so.
